blocks.content: The Mughal Empire was one of the most powerful empires in Indian history. It was founded by Babur in 1526 after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat. The Mughal period is extremely important for competitive examinations such as SSC, SSC, NDA and various State level exams.
1. Foundation of the Mughal Empire

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Babur laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in 1526 after victory in North India.
Humayun succeeded Babur, facing severe political struggle and temporary exile before restoring Mughal rule.
Akbar consolidated the empire through administrative innovations like the Mansabdari system and liberal social policies.
Shah Jahan and Jahangir presided over a period of major artistic, cultural, and architectural achievements.
Aurangzeb expanded the territorial boundaries to their maximum extent, which was followed by the empire's eventual decline.

blocks.content: • Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan, founded the Mughal Empire.
• He defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
• The victory marked the beginning of Mughal rule in India.
• Babur also fought important battles like the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga.
2. Important Mughal Rulers

cells: Lost empire to Sher Shah Suri but later regained it
Known for justice and patronage of arts

blocks.content: • Founder of the Mughal Empire.
• Introduced gunpowder and field artillery in Indian warfare.
• Wrote his autobiography 'Baburnama'.
• Defeated Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa.
4. Humayun
• Son of Babur.
• Defeated by Sher Shah Suri in the Battle of Kannauj.
• Spent years in exile before regaining the throne with Persian support.
• Died in 1556 after falling from the stairs of his library.
5. Akbar the Great
• Became emperor in 1556.
• Defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat.
• Introduced important administrative reforms.
• Started the policy of religious tolerance (Sulh-i-Kul).
• Founded Din-i-Ilahi.
6. Mughal Administration
7. Jahangir
• Son of Akbar.
• Known for the chain of justice (Zanjir-i-Adl).
• British ambassador Sir Thomas Roe visited his court.

rows: Promoted Sulh-i-kul and abolished Jizya tax
Orthodox policies and re-imposition of Jizya tax
Aggressive Southern expansion into the Deccan

blocks.content: 8. Shah Jahan
• Period known for architectural achievements.
• Built the Taj Mahal in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
• Also built Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi.
9. Aurangzeb
• Last powerful Mughal ruler.
• Expanded Mughal territory to its maximum extent.
• Reimposed the Jizya tax on non-Muslims.
10. Mughal Art and Architecture
• Taj Mahal is one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
• Red Fort in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
• Mughal architecture combines Persian, Indian and Islamic styles.
11. Decline of the Mughal Empire
• Weak successors after Aurangzeb.

items: Chronology of Great Mughals (Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb) is frequently tested.
Administrative terms such as Mansabdari and revenue systems from Akbar's reign are core SSC exam topics.
Major architecture built under Shah Jahan and Jahangir frequently appears in art & culture MCQs.

blocks.content: • Rise of regional powers such as Marathas.
• Foreign invasions by Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
• British expansion weakened Mughal authority.
SSC Exam Important Facts
• Mughal Empire founded in 1526 by Babur.
• Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system.
• Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan.
• Sir Thomas Roe visited Jahangir's court.
• Aurangzeb was the last powerful Mughal ruler.
